html:
On 25 December 1978 Vietnam invaded Cambodia after years of Khmer Rouge raids across the border. It took Phnom Penh on 7 January 1979 and drove Pol Pot's forces to the Thai border.

Vietnam set up a new government of former Khmer Rouge defectors, among them Hun Sen. Survivors returned home to a land without money, schools or doctors, and famine followed.

China, the United States and most of the West refused to recognise the new state, and the Khmer Rouge kept Cambodia's seat at the United Nations. China attacked Vietnam in 1979 in punishment. Vietnamese troops left in 1989, opening the way to the UN peace plan. See Cambodian genocide.
sum: On 25 December 1978 Vietnam invaded Cambodia after years of Khmer Rouge raids across the border. It took Phnom Penh on 7 January 1979 and drove Pol Pot's forces to the Thai border.
